sources.entry: BlackHole - Freemium, open-source virtual output/input audio driver for recording/routing internal audio. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ExistentialAudio/BlackHole) [![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/ExistentialAudio/BlackHole)
BlackHole - BlackHole is a modern macOS virtual audio driver that allows applications to pass audio to other applications with zero additional latency.

summary.one_liner: BlackHole is a macOS virtual audio loopback driver that passes audio between applications with zero additional driver latency.
summary.what_it_does: BlackHole installs as a virtual audio device on macOS that lets one application send audio to another, or lets you capture system audio. The README describes builds with 2, 16, 64, 128, and 256 channels, customizable channel count, latency (up to 65536 frames), and hidden devices. It supports sample rates from 8kHz to 768kHz and uses 32-bit float. A mirrored device option can produce separate input-only and output-only virtual devices. Installation is via a downloadable installer or Homebrew (2ch, 16ch, 64ch), with no kernel extensions needed. The README includes user guides for routing audio from Logic Pro X, GarageBand, Audacity, and Reaper to apps like Zoom, Skype, FaceTime, and Google Meet, plus recording system audio through a Multi-Output Device. Developer sections cover building with xcodebuild, renaming and customizing via preprocessor constants, and CI integration.
use_cases: route audio from a DAW into video calls
record system audio on a Mac
send GarageBand or Logic Pro output to Zoom or Google Meet
set up a virtual microphone or speaker for audio apps
monitor and record audio with a multi-output device
how_to_run: Download the latest installer from the project's releases and close all running audio applications
Open and install the package, then restart your system when prompted
Or install via Homebrew: brew install blackhole-2ch (also blackhole-16ch or blackhole-64ch)
To uninstall manually: rm -R /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL/BlackHoleXch.driver, then run sudo killall -9 coreaudiod
notable: Zero additional driver latency, with configurable latency buffer up to 65536 frames
Mirrored device option creates linked input-only and output-only virtual devices
No kernel extensions or changes to system security required
Build-time customization of driver name, bundle ID, icon, channels, and sample rates
caveats: Licensed under GPL-3.0; apps not under GPL-3.0 need a separate license from Existential Audio
Multi-Output and aggregate devices can be buggy, and some apps (Apple Podcasts, Apple Messages, HDHomeRun) are listed as incompatible
macOS does not let you change volume of a Multi-Output device directly
